audit.whatIsWrong: All seven level rows named a side that its own 'why' text contradicts. whys[0] says Q outranges her entire level-1 kit on a 'Skill' row; whys[1] opens 'Even Skirmish' on a Kennen row; whys[2] says her level-3 combo out-trades you on a Kennen row; whys[3] says 'She owns the hard-commit window' on a Skill row; whys[4] says you blow her up on a Skill row; whys[5] says her Sheen spike out-trades you on a Kennen row; whys[6] says 'Genuinely even late' on a Kennen row.
audit.why: The lane really does swing: Kennen owns level 1 on range, Camille owns 3 through 5 once Precision Protocol, Tactical Sweep and Hookshot are all up, Kennen takes level 6 with a flat 120s Slicing Maelstrom against her 140s, she retakes it on Sheen, and the late game splits between her sidelane and his teamfight. The packet levelChart matches all seven rows.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Kennen / Skill / Camille / Camille / Kennen / Camille / Skill in both layers, with phases[2], [3], [5] and [6].why rewritten to state the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers in the full layer, and phases[5].why claimed the first-item window for Kennen when the content layer gives it to Camille.
audit.why: Hookshot 16/15/14/13/12, Precision Protocol 9/8/7/6/5, Tactical Sweep 15/14/13/12/11, The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90. Kennen's flat 120s Maelstrom beats her rank-1 140s, which is precisely why level 6 is his row and first item is hers.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt with the real numbers; phases[3] and [5].why now name Precision Protocol and Tactical Sweep instead of a bare cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot was called a stun in dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].t, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns — it is a knock-up. Adaptive Defenses was never mentioned at all, and it is the single most important interaction here.
audit.why: Riot's text: Hookshot pulls her to a WALL, then leaps off and KNOCKS UP on landing — no wall, no engage, and it is a knock-up not a stun, which changes what you can do about it. Adaptive Defenses gives her a shield sized to her maximum health against the damage type that just hit her, so against Kennen it is specifically a magic shield that eats the front of the burst. Precision Protocol is an auto reset carrying true damage — the attack wind-up is the tell, not the cast.
audit.corrected: report[5].t now states Adaptive Defenses; breakdown.cooldowns states the knock-up, the wall requirement, the auto reset and the true damage; dontsFull[0] and dontsFull[1] carry the wall rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late and report[12].t all called Camille 'he'/'him'.
audit.why: Wrong-gender pronouns read as template filler.

notes: Camille's The Hextech Ultimatum carries a derived 'untargetable' flag that Riot's own description flatly does not support (she dashes to a target champion and anchors them; nothing about untargetability), so the missingInteractions 'untargetable-dodges-burst' headline was NOT written to the page — asserting it would tell the reader to hold a 120s ultimate for a phase that does not exist. Its derived 'channel' flag is likewise absent from the text and was not asserted; the mirror audit already stripped channel wording from the Camille side for the same reason. Both packet suspectNames ('Your Thundering Shuriken', 'Land Thundering Shuriken') are FALSE POSITIVES. All seven level-chart rows were flipped in matched pairs, landing on the packet's chart and on what each whys[N] already said.
